name: goss-b3093595-blind28-ots
instr:
# goss-regen

The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits. The tool takes a written description of how a machine ought to look, examines the machine against that description and announces a verdict, and it now gets that wrong at nearly every stage. Nothing about the descriptions changed and nothing about the machines changed. What follows is everything I have been able to observe from the outside, arranged by what I was doing at the time.

When I ask for a verdict on a description and read back what is announced, a pass in which every single check succeeds is now announced as a failure by several of the reporting styles. The terse one-line summary meant for monitoring plugins prints the failure wording and exits nonzero for a description with nothing wrong in it. The chatty style that prints a line per check prints every one of those lines as succeeding and then exits nonzero anyway. The metrics-shaped rendering exits nonzero for a description that is all successes, all skips or all unknowns, while one that genuinely holds failures still exits one. The terse spec-shaped style has it the other way round: a description that does hold failures exits two instead of one. The plan-and-assertion style declares on its first line a smaller number of assertions than the number of assertion lines it then prints. And checking a description that holds failures without asking for any retries produces text and exit statuses that differ from what the same description used to p
